description:
## Problem
Ranked cohorts exist at scale factor 10, where TPC-H, TPC-DS and SSB have no row-count references. The single reader, the generator and the SF 0.01, 0.1 and 1 references land first in crr-v0 (owner decision 9, 2026-11-25). The SF 10 TPC-DS reference must land after the integrity checks (crr-v2): with the old validator, seeded SF 10 TPC-DS runs would move from ranked to refused.

## Change
- SF 10 references for TPC-H, TPC-DS and SSB through the crr-v0 reader and generator. Each has an integrity section from at least 256 draws covering both generation paths (owner decision 1). Exact per-stream counts are keyed by dsqgen RNGSEED and STREAMS index, or qgen seed, never by stream number. No four-seed parameter_sensitive_query_ids.
- Each reference records how it was made: generator, data checksum and stamp, reference engines and versions, date. Above the scales the TPC answer sets cover it is labelled 'agreement with <engine>', not the specification's answer.
- Guard: a ranked cohort for these three benchmarks without a reference fails CI.
- Do not reintroduce the staged text 'throughput rows and other seeds are skipped'.

## Decision gates
- Reference engine default: DuckDB SQL on the same generated data; a second engine (DataFusion) must agree on a 64-draw subset. If they disagree on any query, stop and report the query; do not pick one.
- Generating SF 10 references is heavy work (about 1.5 to 3 hours): make heavy-run only, with command, maximum run time and log path announced.
- TPC-H SF 10 data from the defective generator (known_defects defective-macdbgen-addresses) must not be used.
- If a seeded TPC-DS SF 10 run records not_validated or is refused, stop.

## Guardrails (apply to every step of this plan)
- Fix the root cause for every platform and benchmark. No rule, check, exception, label or test may name a platform or a version matrix; only the pvm items may name Polars, and only to run and stage that run's files.
- Never edit a stored result file. Stored outcomes change only through the rule; any change shows in the committed snapshot diff (scripts/corpus_compliance_snapshot.py) and is explained per bundle in the pull request body.
- No new stored class value. No reader decides anything from benchmark.compliance_class, conformance_class or summary.tpc_metrics.suppressed.
- One implementation per concept: reuse existing helpers; make duplicate-check-delta stays at +0; no second copy of the rule, the roll-up, the row decision or the qualification comparator.
- No explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check). User-facing changes add a changelog.d fragment; never edit CHANGELOG.md.
- Heavy work only through make heavy-run, after make heavy-status, with command, maximum run time and log path announced first. No live cloud runs. Never touch the lock, set BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK, BENCHBOX_HEAVY_ADMIT=force or BENCHBOX_HEAVY_WATCHDOG=off.
- Work in a linked worktree on the step's feature batch. Each batch is one pull request; run the local review before opening it; fix hosted-review findings. If the hosted review cannot complete, split the pull request so a reviewer can read it (owner, 2026-11-24). Never post a stand-in or adjudication, except on published-results pull requests, which follow the owner decision of 2026-11-24: an independent review with no Critical or Required findings, then a stand-in that cites it.
- Paths and line numbers were read on 2026-11-25 at the corpus rule head; re-read before editing and report drift instead of guessing.
- At a decision gate, follow the recorded owner decision. If its stop condition is met, stop and report to the owner; never substitute a different decision.
- Owner decisions: crr-00-corpus-rule-remediation-plan context, entries of 2026-11-22, 2026-11-24 and 2026-11-25. Design: the spec-faithful validation plan summarized in crr-00 (qualification test, integrity checks, official-mode sequence).
